science.title: Nanoparticle properties shape protein coats that guide cell entry and immune evasion
science.description: A new study has revealed molecular rules governing how nanoparticles interact with biological systems, showing how their physicochemical properties shape protein corona (PC) formation and influence biological outcomes. The findings provide a framework for designing nanomedicines with more predictable biological identities.

science.title: Immune system protein is a cancer killer on its own, new study shows
science.description: For decades, scientists have known that a protein made by T cells and natural killer (NK) cells in the immune system, called perforin, can kill tumor cells by punching a hole in the cell wall and injecting proteases called granzymes, which kill the cell. Now, new work led by researchers at the University of Michigan Health Rogel Cancer Center found that tumor cells could be killed even when major granzymes were missing.

science.title: Ghostly Cat's Head Nebula lurks within sight of NASA's Hubble, Webb
science.description: NASA's Hubble and James Webb Space Telescopes have captured a hauntingly dynamic star-forming scene, like a spectral form rising out of a cold mist. It lies within the vast Carina Nebula, a diffuse star-forming region located about 7,500 light-years away from Earth. The small, select area both telescopes observed is nicknamed the Cat's Head Nebula because of its resemblance to a cat sitting with its back toward the viewer. The "head" of the cat is turned to the right, revealing a glowing eye.

science.title: NASA's PESTO Investigation: Space-Grown Wheat Outperforms Earth Counterparts in Height and Development

science.title: Martian meteorite found in the Sahara is 4.1 billion years old
science.description: A meteorite discovered in Mali’s Sahara Desert may be among the oldest known rocks from Mars. Scientists say the 4.1-billion-year-old rock offers evidence that water interacted with the Martian crust during the planet’s early history.

science.title: Zombie bacteria keep building DNA after death
